title: TYP: Improve support for unbounded tuples of `None` in array scalar `__getitem__()`
body:
### PR summary

#### Updated summary

On current `main` there are `generic.__getitem__()` and `void.__getitem__()` overloads for tuples of `None` with all possible lengths. But because the Python typing specification does not require type checkers to expand unbounded tuples then the annotations can be expected to work only with tuples the lengths of which are known statically. In practice arguments with the type `tuple[None, ...]` cause [type checking errors](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/32763#issuecomment-5800603791) with mypy, pyrefly and ty. This PR updates the overloads so that unbounded tuples of `None` can be type checked too.

#### Original summary

There already are tests for array scalar `__getitem__()` annotations using tuples of `None` with statically known lengths. The first commit here adds tests for variadic `None` tuples, which reveal that at least mypy has trouble in such cases. The second commit updates annotations of `generic.__getitem__()` and `void.__getitem__()` so that variadic `None` tuples can be type checked well enough (with mypy).~

I suspect variadic `None` tuples might be relevant in cases that look something like
```
def f(..., shape: Shape, ...):
    ...
    some_ufunc(...)[shape]
    ...
```
where `Shape` might be a type union containing `tuple[None, ...]`. Most importantly, the updated annotations make it clear that if the `some_ufunc()` call can return an array scalar and `shape` can be an empty tuple then `some_ufunc(...)[shape]` is not guaranteed to be an array but can be an array scalar instead.

No AI tools used
